issues.description: Deprecation message contains a typo ('stlib') in the docstring directive.
issues.detail: In falcon/testing/helpers.py, the new `.. deprecated:: 4.3` block says 'Use the stlib's' instead of 'stdlib's'. This typo will be rendered in the published Sphinx docs and is user-facing. Worth fixing before merge to avoid an immediate follow-up doc PR.

issues.description: Deprecation decorator order may mask the contextmanager protocol.
issues.detail: `@falcon.util.deprecated` is applied above `@contextlib.contextmanager`, so the outermost wrapper is the deprecation wrapper, which typically returns the generator object directly. Confirm that `falcon.util.deprecated` preserves return values (so `with redirected(...)` still works); the new test only exercises the happy path with no exception inside the block.

issues.description: News fragment classified as 'misc' rather than 'deprecation'.
issues.detail: Falcon's towncrier setup typically has a dedicated 'deprecation' fragment type. Using `2569.misc.rst` for a user-visible deprecation likely buries this change in the misc section of the changelog instead of the deprecations section. Consider renaming to `2569.deprecation.rst` if that fragment type exists.

issues.description: Deprecation test does not assert the warning fires only once or at call time.
issues.detail: test_deprecated_redirected in tests/test_testing.py uses `pytest.warns` around the whole `with` block, so it cannot distinguish whether the warning is emitted on call vs. on enter/exit. Tightening with `len(record) == 1` and checking it fires at the `redirected(...)` call would make the contract explicit.

issues.description: Default mutable-ish stdout/stderr bound at import time still inherited by deprecation wrapper.
issues.detail: `redirected(stdout=sys.stdout, stderr=sys.stderr)` captures the streams at import time. This pre-existed, but since the function is now wrapped by `deprecated`, double-check that pytest's capture machinery still sees the right streams when the test imports `testing` before capture is set up; the new test relies on explicit StringIO so it's fine, but a note in the docstring would help users migrating.

review.summary: The PR cleanly deprecates `falcon.testing.redirected` with a decorator, docstring directive, news fragment, and a regression test. Main concerns are a typo ('stlib') that will render in published docs, the news fragment being categorized as 'misc' instead of 'deprecation', and verifying the decorator stacking with `@contextlib.contextmanager` does not interfere with the context-manager protocol. The test coverage is minimal — happy path only, no exception-propagation case. Overall low risk but worth a small polish pass.
